title: The Velographer | Episode 195 - This Budget Aero Bike Shocked Me | Alvas DA54 Review

takeaways.text: Quoted at A$5,200 retail in Australia (about US$4,500 by his estimate) with a T700/T800 carbon aero frame, integrated cockpit and 60 mm hooked carbon Helux wheels.
The stock size-S bike weighed 8.4 kg with Dura-Ace pedals; after swapping wheels, saddle, cassette and tape it was 7.77 kg with pedals, mounts and computer.

The aero seatpost uses a compression-plug clamp and did not slip; the integrated cockpit came with an 80 mm stem and 400 mm drops (about 300 mm at the hoods); T47 bottom bracket and 165 mm cranks on the small size.
The build is full Shimano Ultegra 12-speed Di2 including chain and cassette, with no substituted parts.
Steering is sharp yet stable above 60 km/h on a descent with no rattles or wobbles; the stock saddle was comfortable for 100 km.

disclosure: How the bike was obtained is not stated; the presenter is sponsored by a wheel brand whose wheels he fitted after the stock test.
summary: An Australian rider's first 160 km on a size-S ALVAS DA54 with Shimano Ultegra Di2 and 60 mm Helux wheels, including stock and modified weights.
